title: The domain vocabulary for a multiplayer coding agent
author: pratos with Claude Code
summary: Greenhouse has words for planning but none for the agent's own work, the live room, or the workspace where code changes. This plan names them, once, in the glossary and in `packages/schema`, so people, code and the agent say the same thing as the product grows onto pi-durable, Durable Objects and Containers. Library words stay inside the adapters that use them.
current: The glossary has eight nouns across Planning and Identity (`docs/GLOSSARY.md`). It already contradicts itself in two places, and three of its schemas do not exist yet. The stack under it brings its own words, and many of them collide: *session* means six things across pi-durable, the Sandbox SDK and auth, *agent* is a configuration in pi-durable but an actor here, and Amp's *thread* is a unit of work while ours is a comment thread.
discoveries: Plan is defined as "a document" while banning *document* (`docs/GLOSSARY.md:28,30`), and Exploration is "an agent thread", which is not our Thread (`docs/GLOSSARY.md:23`).
The verb list omits Post, Record, Start and Report, which events already use (`docs/GLOSSARY.md:51`, `packages/domain/src/thread/decider.ts:10-13`).
`rationale` is read by the upcaster but is in neither the glossary nor the Decision schema (`packages/domain/src/upcast/index.ts:4-12`).
Chopin's product noun is *document*; *Plan* is its UI tab label, *room* is internal, and its hosted agent is the *Planner* (githubnext/chopin `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`).
Chopin calls what an exploration returns a *finding* (kinds research, spike, ask) and the one-sentence reason on a decision its *why* (`docs/decisions.md`).
pi-durable's *run* is the turns from one input to its final answer, the same as what people mean by the agent is running (pi-durable README, Concepts).
The Sandbox SDK 1.0 removed *sessions* and *preview URLs* as 0.x had them, so neither should become a domain word from that source.

The labels *decision report*, *option explorer*, *state machine explorer*, *trace views*, *parallel lookahead* and *pre-handoff exploration* do not appear in Maggie Appleton's talk or the Chopin sources. Her own terms are *boundary objects*, *interactive report*, *explore the terrain ahead of time* and *made meaningful contact with the important parts of reality*.
endState: `docs/GLOSSARY.md` names four contexts with every noun, command and event the next phases of Greenhouse need, each entry with where the word was seen and the synonyms it replaces. Each noun has an Effect Schema in `packages/schema`. A translation table says which library word maps to which product word and where library words may appear. `just glossary-check` fails on a library word outside an adapter, an unknown verb, or a missing schema. `just glossary` renders the vocabulary as a map you can step through.
notDoing: Implementing Runs, Rooms or Workspaces. This plan names them; the deciders and screens are their own plans.
Renaming kernel words like Decider, Message and Rejection. They are the event-sourcing kernel's own words, internal to `packages/domain/src/kernel.ts`.
Adopting Chopin's identifiers. We borrow a word when users already say it, and leave Chopin's wire protocol where it is.
Rewriting the workshop page. Only the Appleton attribution is corrected, in the page and the viz-explainer skill.
approach: Fix what the glossary already gets wrong before adding to it, so new words land on a consistent base. Then draw the contexts and the boundary, because the four decisions below are all about where a word lives. Write the entries and schemas next, then make the check enforce them, and finish by rendering the vocabulary so it can be shown and reviewed by looking.

spec.question: Which words live where, and where do they get translated?
spec.diagram:
flowchart LR
  subgraph planning["Planning"]
    PLN["Plan · Block · Thread · Reply · Decision"]
    EXP["Exploration · Finding · Artifact"]
  end
  subgraph together["Working together"]
    RM["Room · Presence"]
    PA["Participant · person or Agent"]
  end
  subgraph work["Agent work"]
    RUN["Run · Turn · Tool call"]
    RES["Checkpoint · Interruption · Steer · Follow-up"]
  end
  subgraph place["Workspace"]
    WS["Workspace · Repo · Branch · Preview"]
  end
  PD["pi-durable words · Conversation, Entry, Submission, Task"]
  CF["Cloudflare words · Durable Object, Container, Sandbox"]
  PA -- "acts in" --> RM
  RM -- "is opened on" --> PLN
  PA -- "starts" --> RUN
  RUN -- "reports" --> EXP
  RUN -- "survives a crash through" --> RES
  RUN -- "works in" --> WS
  PD -. "translated at the edge" .-> RUN
  CF -. "translated at the edge" .-> WS

steps.caption: Planning keeps the words people write and decide with, unchanged from today.
Working together names who is here and that a person and the Agent act alike.
Agent work names what the agent does, so people can see a run and its interruptions.
The Workspace is where the agent changes code, a repo and a branch it can preview.
Library words stop at the edge, and each one has a single product word on the other side.

spec.question: What can a Run be, from asked to answered?

meta.source: pi-durable run and task states, in product words

spec.diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Queued: StartRun
  Queued --> Running: RunStarted
  Running --> Waiting: ToolCallStarted
  Waiting --> Running: ToolCallFinished
  Waiting --> Interrupted: process stopped
  Interrupted --> Running: RunResumed
  Running --> Answered: RunAnswered
  Running --> Failed: RunFailed
  Running --> Stopped: StopRun
  Answered --> [*]
  Failed --> [*]
  Stopped --> [*]

steps.caption: Someone asks; if the agent is busy, the ask waits as a Steer or a Follow-up.
The Run starts and takes Turns, each one a model reply and its tool calls.
A tool call is running, and the Run waits for its result.
If the process dies here, the Run is marked Interrupted and keeps everything it committed.
It resumes from the last Checkpoint, and a tool that is safe to repeat runs again.
A Run ends answered, failed or stopped, and each end is a fact in the log.

decisions.why: We recommend *Run*. It is how people already describe an agent at work, pi-durable means the same thing by it, and it is the only option with no collision in the glossary.

decisions.question: Where may pi-durable and Cloudflare words appear?
decisions.why: We recommend translating at the edge. pi-durable is experimental and renames things between releases, so keeping its words inside two folders means an upgrade never renames the domain.

phases.name: Fix what the glossary gets wrong today
phases.goal: The existing entries agree with themselves and with the code. Plan no longer defines itself with a banned word, Exploration no longer borrows Thread, the verb list matches the events, and the Decision's reason has a name.

changes.intent: Redefine Plan without *document*, define Exploration as work that tries one option, add Post, Record, Start and Report to the verbs, and give Decision a *why*.
Add the optional `why` field to Decision, matching what the upcaster already reads.
Rename `rationale` to `why` in the v1 to v2 upcaster and its expect snapshot.
Attribute boundary objects and interactive reports to Appleton, and the pattern labels to this workshop.
Same attribution fix in the planning section.

manual.text: Read the Plan, Exploration and Decision entries aloud; none uses a word its own Not line bans.

phases.name: Draw the contexts and the boundary
phases.goal: The glossary has four contexts (Planning, Working together, Agent work, Workspace) and a translation table that maps every library word a user could meet to one product word, or marks it internal. The decisions above are recorded.

changes.intent: Add the contexts and a Boundary section per context: library word, product word, and the folders where the library word may appear.

contract.code:
## Boundary: Agent work
| Library word | Product word | Allowed in |
|---|---|---|
| pi-durable run | Run | packages/agent |
| pi-durable Submission, Entry, Task, Harness | internal | packages/agent |
| pi-durable Agent | Setup | packages/agent |

phases.name: Write the new words and their schemas
phases.goal: Every new noun has an entry with a definition a user would nod at, a Seen in line naming its source, its banned synonyms, and an Effect Schema. Run's lifecycle is named state by state.

changes.intent: Add Run, Turn, Tool call, Checkpoint, Interruption, Steer, Follow-up, Setup, Finding, Room, Presence, Workspace, Repo, Branch and Preview, each with Seen in and Not lines.

phases.name: Make the check enforce the boundary
phases.goal: `just glossary-check` fails when a library word appears outside its allowed folders, when a command or event uses a verb that is not in the verb list, or when an entry names a schema that does not exist. CI runs it.
